checklist: Confirm at least two independent price sources before trusting a price band (PRS §5 Evidence Hierarchy)
Never treat a single review or a single supplier quote as representative — look for a pattern across multiple sources
Distinguish Verified facts from Estimated, Assumed, and Unknown ones explicitly — never let a confident guess pass as a fact (PRS §17)
Check GST/HSN classification with a professional before finalizing pricing
Always request a physical sample before committing to a supplier's MOQ
evidence_priority_notes: Government and manufacturer sources outrank marketplace listings, which outrank customer reviews, which outrank forum/social chatter (PRS §5)
AI reasoning without a real source behind it is the weakest evidence tier — treat it as a starting hypothesis, not a conclusion
common_pitfalls: Anchoring on the first price or quote seen instead of gathering a real range
Treating a low review count as 'not enough evidence to worry about' rather than 'not enough evidence to trust either way'
Skipping manual verification on Supplier/Compliance items just because the rest of the research looked solid

checklist: Verify BIS/CRS certification status before sourcing at volume
Test compatibility claims against the specific device models advertised, not just the general category
Check for counterfeit or trademark risk if the product resembles a known branded accessory
evidence_priority_notes: Marketplace review complaints about 'stopped working' or 'not compatible' are a stronger signal here than in most categories — weight them accordingly
common_pitfalls: Assuming a supplier's compatibility claim is accurate without independent verification
Underestimating return rate — electronics accessories return at nearly double the typical cross-category rate

checklist: Confirm CDSCO compliance for any formulated product
Review ingredient-list transparency against the supplier's certificate
Check for allergy or patch-test complaints in existing reviews, not just star ratings
evidence_priority_notes: A high star rating with buried allergy complaints in the review text is a real risk — read review text, not only the aggregate score
common_pitfalls: Treating 'natural' or 'organic' claims as verified without a supplier certificate
Underweighting formulation-safety risk relative to packaging or logistics risk

checklist: Confirm toy safety / BIS certification before sourcing
Read safety-related complaints in full — do not rely on star rating alone
evidence_priority_notes: A single credible safety complaint should outweigh many positive but safety-irrelevant reviews
common_pitfalls: Treating this as a normal commodity category — safety stakes are categorically higher here
Under-investing in manual compliance verification just because the product 'looks like every other listing'

checklist: Verify size-chart accuracy against actual garment measurements, not just the printed size label
Check fabric composition claims against the supplier's certificate
Review fit and true-to-size complaints specifically
evidence_priority_notes: Return-rate evidence matters more here than in almost any other category — apparel's 18%+ typical return rate makes size/fit research disproportionately high-value
common_pitfalls: Copying a competitor's size chart without verifying it matches your own supplier's actual cut
Underestimating return cost in the profit model specifically for apparel
